newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Hermis Bank hit on Lithuania bourse, Birzai up again.
newsitem.headline: Hermis Bank hit on Lithuania bourse, Birzai up again.

text.p: Leading commercial bank Hermis Bank eased on a quiet Lithuanian bourse and the main market index inched down on Wednesday, dealers said.
Overall central market volume was only 900,000 litas and the group A index dipped by 2.94 points to 2,411.94.
Hermis Bank, one of the leading commercial banks, was the day's biggest casuality, falling 10 percent to 175.50 litas in trade of 86,700 litas.
The session's few gainers included Birzai Dairy, which advanced to 10.20 litas from 10.00 litas with 2,550 litas worth of shares changing hands.
Hermis Bank recently received a good rating from Thomson BankWatch and is expecting a profit of 25 million litas in 1996 after a loss in 1995.
But dealers said the market is sceptical about this figure and some feel that the final audited results will be lower.

"There is a feeling that the bank's bad loan portfolio could bring the profit figure down somewhat, although it is still expected to be good. This has reduced the demand in Hermis shares," one broker told Reuters.
Lithuanian Sea Shipping also lost ground, slipping by 2.14 percent to 6.85 litas in turnover of almost 83,000 litas.
Birzai has been gaining steadily, rising about a third in the past week despite an unaudited statement of results for 1996 that fell short of market expectations.

The dairy, which issued a $6 million GDR subscription late last year, is regarded as one of the best managed companies in Lithuania, a country with a strong tradition in dairy and other agricultural products.
Block trades on Wednesday amounted to over one million litas and volume on the secondary T-bill market was also just over one million litas.
